For steering text-to-image models with a human preference reward, we find that fk steering a 0.8B parameter model outperforms a 2.6B parameter fine-tuned model on prompt fidelity, with faster sampling and no training .

For steering text diffusion models with rewards for text quality and specific text attributes, we find that fk steering generates lower perplexity, more linguistically acceptable outputs and enables gradient-free control of attributes like toxicity.
Our results demonstrate that inference-time scaling and steering of diffusion models – even with off-the-shelf rewards – can provide significant sample quality gains and controllability benefits.
We demonstrate that fk steering enables new choices of potentials, samplers, and reward models that can improve performance across many tasks.
fk steering with just k = 4 k=4 particles outperforms fine-tuning on prompt fidelity and aesthetic quality, without making use of reward gradients.
We also steer text diffusion models to generate higher quality samples that have more competitive linguistic acceptability and perplexity to those sampled from auto-regressive models.
